Plant spring-flowering perinneas

Plant these in early or very end Autumn to benefit their growth over winter months, which will lead in spring to robust flowering stems, a vibrant and early season garden show and less risk in case a winter cold snaps or freezes them as a plant already growing back is often hardiest against frost.
Choose healthy looking divisions that can have been lifted with tongs and gently split, to get at your chosen size plant -  the divisions will likely not all grow at one speed.
Loosly work a tined rake into soil that will get about your 60 x28 x5 inches deep.
